claims: Gary Woodland underwent surgery in September 2023 to remove a benign lesion (tumor) from his brain.
The benign lesion (tumor) was causing partial seizures, fear, and anxiety.
The tumor was located on the part of his brain that controls fear and anxiety, according to the Jacksonville.com article and the Yahoo Sports Canada article.
The tumor resulted in symptoms like tremors, jolting awake, and significant fear, according to the Jacksonville.com article and the Yahoo Sports Canada article.
Following the surgery, Gary Woodland was diagnosed with Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD).
Gary Woodland has been managing severe anxiety, fear of death, and ongoing mental and emotional struggles.
In early 2026, Woodland revealed that about a year prior, he was diagnosed with PTSD stemming from the trauma of his diagnosis and surgery, as reported by the PGA Tour article and People.com.
Woodland noted that he still struggles with PTSD daily, as reported by the PGA Tour article and People.com.
Woodland returned to competition in January 2024.
The 2026 Houston Open was Woodland's first victory since the surgery, noted by the BBC.
